# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 27 ON THE SAND BAR

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

It was the following morning when Adrian Treleaven departed Seven Gulls. Nell visited to check on Lorna that evening, yet she discovered no one there. Locked up tight, the house showed no illumination in a single window. A house stripped of its soul was what it resembled. Lorna failed to hurry over the next day—an omen Nell considered negative.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0000 }

Because Hugh needed to head to the fishing cove during the evening, Nell went along in the vehicle with him as far as the Point, planning to spend some time with Captain Saul. However, the immense beacon, slicing its beams through the autumn evening's fog, was being tended by Hector Garrick, and Captain Saul was absent.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0001 }

“What is your plan?” Hugh inquired. “Will you join me?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0002 }

“To the cove I do not wish to go—yet I will cross the channel alongside you, and wander upon the sandy beach until your return. Tonight, the rocky coast is excessively slick and forbidding.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0003 }

On the bar's sands by herself, Nell surrendered to the night's strange, enchanting mood. September felt unusually warm, and a dense fog had marked the late afternoon; nevertheless, the full moon partially diminished the mist, converting the gulf, the harbor, and the nearby coasts into a bizarre, whimsical, imaginary realm of faint silver haze, where all objects appeared like phantoms. Moving down the channel, Captain Josiah Crawford’s black schooner, loaded with potatoes destined for Bluenose ports, seemed to be a ghost vessel heading toward a distant, unmapped territory that continually pulled away and could never be attained. The shouts from hidden gulls above sounded like the wails of lost sailors' spirits. Small tendrils of foam blowing over the sand resembled magical creatures slipping out from underwater caverns. The large, slumping sand-dunes appeared as the resting giants from an ancient northern legend. Pale lights flickering over the harbor acted as misleading signals along a fairytale shoreline. Nell entertained herself with a century of imaginative thoughts while she roamed in the mist. Wandering by herself on this spellbound beach felt wonderful, romantic, and mysterious.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0004 }

Yet was she by herself? An object emerged in the fog ahead of her—assumed a distinct shape—and unexpectedly advanced in her direction over the sands rippled by waves.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0005 }

“Lorna!” Nell cried out, thoroughly astonished. “What in the world brings you—HERE—this evening?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0006 }

“If we are on the subject, what in the world are YOU doing in this place?” asked Lorna, attempting a laugh. It proved to be a failed attempt. A very pale and exhausted appearance marked her face; nevertheless, the love locks beneath her scarlet cap were forming curls around her face and eyes that resembled small, glistening gold rings.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0007 }

“I am awaiting Hugh, who is currently over at the Cove. My plan had been to remain at the lighthouse, however Captain Saul is absent.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0008 }

“Well, I arrived at this place since I desired to walk—and walk—and WALK,” Lorna said with uneasiness. “I was unable to on the rocky coast—the water had risen too far and the boulders trapped me. It was necessary for me to come here—otherwise I would have lost my mind, I believe. I used Captain Saul’s flat to row across the passage. An hour has passed while I have been here. Come—come—we must walk. Remaining still is impossible for me. Oh, Nell!”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0009 }

“Lorna, my darling, what is wrong?” inquired Nell, even though she was already far too aware.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0010 }

“I am unable to inform you—do not request it of me. Your knowing would not bother me—it is my desire that you were aware—yet I am unable to inform you—I am unable to inform a single person. I have acted like such an idiot, Nell—and oh, being an idiot causes such extreme agony. No other thing in existence brings as much distress.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0011 }

Her laughter was bitter. Around her, Nell slid an arm.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0012 }

“Lorna, have you come to feel affection for Mr. Treleaven?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0013 }

Lorna spun around in a passionate manner.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0014 }

“In what way did you find out?” she exclaimed. “Nell, in what way did you find out? Oh, does my face display it for all to perceive? Is it that obvious?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0015 }

“Nay, nay. I—I am unable to explain to you the way I was aware. In some manner, it simply entered my thoughts. Lorna, do not regard me in that fashion!”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0016 }

“Are you despising me?” Lorna asked, her voice quiet and intense. “Is it your belief that I am evil—not act as a woman should? Or am I merely a complete idiot in your eyes?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0017 }

“I do not consider you to be any of those things. Come on, my dear, let us simply discuss this in a sensible manner, just as we would discuss any other major life crisis. You have been dwelling on this matter and permitted yourself to fall into an unhealthy perspective regarding it. You are aware that you possess a slight inclination to react this way to anything that turns out badly, and you gave me your word that you would strive against it.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0018 }

“But—oh, it’s so—so humiliating,” Lorna whispered. “To be in love with him—without him asking—and at a time when I’m not at liberty to love anyone.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0019 }

“It contains no disgrace. However, your growing affection for Adrian causes me great regret, since, given the present circumstances, your sorrow will merely deepen.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0020 }

“I didn’t LEARN to care,” Lorna said, continuing her walk and expressing herself with great passion. “If that had been the case, I might have stopped it. Such a thought never crossed my mind until a week ago, on that day when he informed me that his book was completed and he would have to leave shortly. At that moment—then I realized it. It was as though a dreadful blow had been dealt to me. I remained silent—speech was impossible for me—yet I have no idea how my expression appeared. I am terrified that my face gave me away. Oh, dying of shame would be my fate if I believed he was aware—or even harbored a suspicion.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0021 }

Hindered by what she had deduced from her talk with Adrian, Nell remained unhappily quiet. Lorna continued to talk passionately, appearing to gain comfort from speaking.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0022 }

“All through this summer, Nell, my happiness was greater than it had ever been before. My belief was that this stemmed from everything being resolved between us, and that our bond was what rendered existence so lovely and complete again. To an extent, it WAS—yet not entirely—no, far from entirely. The reason for everything feeling so changed is clear to me now. Now, however, it has completely ended—and his departure has happened. Nell, how am I to go on living? Upon returning inside the house earlier today following his departure, the loneliness hit me as if I had been struck across the face.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0023 }

“In time, it will not appear as difficult, dear,” stated Nell, who continuously experienced the suffering of her companions so deeply that uttering smooth, effortless words of solace was impossible for her. In addition, recalling how well-intentioned statements had pained her during her own grief, she felt fearful.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0024 }

“Oh, it appears to me that it will become more difficult continuously,” Lorna stated in misery. “There is nothing for me to anticipate. Day after day will arrive—and his return will not happen—he is never coming back. Oh, whenever I reflect on the fact that he will never be seen by me again, it feels like my heartstrings have been seized by a large, cruel hand and are being torn out. Formerly, a long time in the past, love was dreamed of by me—and my thought was that it had to be lovely—and NOW—it resembles THIS. His departure yesterday morning was marked by such coldness and detachment. 'Good-bye, Mrs. Vane’ was uttered by him using the most frigid tone possible—as though friendship had not even existed between us—as though I possessed no meaning to him whatsoever. My knowledge is that I do not—his caring was not desired by me—nevertheless, he COULD have shown a bit more kindness.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0025 }

“Oh, I wish Hugh would come,” Nell thought. Torn between her pity for Lorna and the need to prevent any disclosure of Adrian’s secret, she understood the reason his farewell was so chilly—the reason it lacked the warmth their strong comradeship required—yet she was unable to inform Lorna.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0026 }

“Nell, I couldn’t prevent it—I really couldn’t prevent it,” wretched Lorna said.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0027 }

“I am aware of that.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0028 }

“Are you holding me so greatly at fault?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0029 }

“I do not hold you responsible in the least.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0030 }

“And you will not—you will not inform Hugh?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0031 }

“Lorna! Is it your belief that I would commit an act like that?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0032 }

“Well, I am uncertain—Hugh and you are such CLOSE FRIENDS. Telling him all the details seems unavoidable to me.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0033 }

“I will share every detail regarding my personal affairs—indeed I will. However, I refuse to reveal what my friends keep hidden.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0034 }

“I couldn’t let HIM be aware. Yet I’m pleased that YOU are aware. I would be filled with guilt if I kept anything from you out of shame. I trust Miss Winifred doesn’t discover it. At times I get the feeling that those dreadful, gentle brown eyes she has gaze right into my soul. Oh, I desire that this fog would refrain from ever clearing—I desire to remain within it for all time, concealed from all creation. I fail to understand how I can continue living. This summer was so packed with activity. Not for one second was I ever lonely. Prior to the arrival of Adrian, there were awful instances—after I was alongside you and Hugh—and subsequently was forced to depart from you. The pair of you would stroll off side by side and I would stroll off ALL BY MYSELF. Once Adrian arrived, he was constantly present to accompany me back home—the two of us would giggle and converse just as you and Hugh did—I experienced no further desolate, jealous instances. And AT THIS MOMENT! Oh, indeed, I’ve acted like a fool. Let us stop discussing my foolishness. I will never weary you with it any more.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0035 }

“Hugh is present, and you will return alongside us,” declared Nell, who possessed no desire to permit Lorna to roam unchaperoned across the sand-bar during a night like this and in a state like hers. “Our boat holds sufficient space for a trio, and the flat can be towed in the rear.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0036 }

“Oh, I guess I have to accept being the third wheel once more,” poor Lorna stated, giving another harsh laugh. “Pardon me, Nell—I was being awful. I should feel grateful—and I AM—for having a pair of great friends who happily include me as a third. Ignore my horrible remarks. It feels as though I am merely a single huge ache everywhere, and every single thing causes me suffering.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0037 }

“Lorna appeared extremely silent this evening, did she not?” remarked Hugh, as soon as he and Nell arrived at their house. “Whatever was she up to by herself over on the sandbar?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0038 }

“Oh, she was exhausted—and you are aware that she enjoys visiting the coast following one of Rufus’s difficult days.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0039 }

“It is such a shame she did not encounter and wed a man such as Treleaven years back,” pondered Hugh. “An ideal pair is what they would have been, wouldn't they?”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0040 }

“For pity’s sake, Hugh, don’t develop into a match-maker. It’s an abominable profession for a man,” exclaimed Nell somewhat sharply, fearful that Hugh would stumble upon the truth were he to continue in that vein.
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0041 }

“Bless us, Nell-girl, I’m not matchmaking,” Hugh protested, taken aback somewhat by how she sounded. “I was merely reflecting on a thing that might have been.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0042 }

“Well, refrain from doing so. You are wasting your time,” remarked Nell. Following that, she abruptly stated:
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0043 }

“Oh, Hugh, I want all people to enjoy the same happiness that we have.”
{: #nw-v04-c27-p0044 }
